hook: The last great Mughal emperor, who ruled India at its largest.

pages.x: Aurangzeb was born in 1618, a son of Shah Jahan. At 14, at a court show, a war elephant charged at him; the boy stood his ground and struck it with his spear. His father showered him with gold.
When Shah Jahan fell ill in 1657, his four sons fought for the throne. Aurangzeb beat them all, had his eldest brother Dara Shikoh executed, and locked his father up in Agra Fort.

He reigned for 49 years and conquered the sultanates of Bijapur and Golconda in the south. His empire covered almost the whole of the subcontinent, the largest it ever was, and India was one of the richest lands on Earth.

A devout Sunni Muslim, he lived simply and is said to have paid for his own needs by copying the Quran and sewing prayer caps. He enforced Islamic law, brought back the tax on non-Muslims and destroyed some Hindu temples, which turned many against him.
His great enemy was Shivaji, leader of the Marathas. In 1666 Shivaji, held under house arrest in Agra, escaped by hiding in one of the huge baskets of sweets he sent out each day as gifts.

Aurangzeb spent his last 26 years at war in the Deccan against the Marathas, a war he could never win. He died in 1707 at 88, writing: "I came alone and I go as a stranger." He asked for a simple grave open to the sky.

Aurangzeb ruled the Mughal Empire at its greatest size, but his wars and harsh religious policies wore it out, and within decades of his death it broke apart. He is still one of the most debated figures in Indian history.
